Subject: LLM key handling & timeline — follow-up from demo

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo this morning — the latency/cost numbers were helpful. Two quick asks from our side so we can move the procurement thread along with legal and infra: a consolidated list of your encryption modes and a short ops playbook for BYOK deployment options.

Can you confirm the following items? I've numbered them so legal/infra can make decisions against each:

1) In-transit: you said TLS 1.2+ with mTLS support — do you support customer-provided certs and mutual TLS to your private deployment (VPC/on-prem)?

2) At-rest: what cipher and key length do you use by default for hosted and dedicated? Is AES-256-GCM used for all persisted artifacts (models, snapshots, logs)?

3) KMS/HSM options: list the supported KMS integrations (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and whether you support external HSMs for key material originating outside cloud providers. Is there a recommended model for our payments workload (we need an HSM-backed KMS and separation of duties).

4) BYOK workflow: what are the steps for us to bring our keys (rotate/rollover) and what level of access do Redwood ops have to keys or key-encrypting-keys? Do you publish any attestation around key custody?

5) Audit and logs: what log events are available for key usage and cryptographic operations? Can we get a dedicated log stream (syslog/CloudWatch/Stackdriver) and what is the retention/retention-by-subscriber options?

6) Data residency and retention: can you confirm where backups and persisted artifacts will live for a private deployment? If we choose hosted, can we pin to a specific region and get a data residency SLA?

To help us, I've attached our initial questionnaire (finedge-security-questions.xlsx). It would be ideal to get a short one-page runbook and the KMS options doc by EOD Friday so legal has something to review before our security committee meeting next week.

Proposed next step: 30 min technical deep-dive with your security engineer + our infra (we can do Wed 5/16 10–10:30 PT or Thu 5/17 14–14:30 PT). Please let me know which slot works.

Thanks —
Sara Khan
Director, Product Security | FinEdge

Sara — really appreciate the clear list. Recap + proposed owners below so we have an actionable plan. I've attached a short summary of our KMS/HSM options (redwood-kms-options.pdf) and a two-page BYOK runbook draft.

Quick answers to your numbered items and owners: 

1) In-transit: Yes — hosted and private support TLS 1.2+; private (VPC/on-prem) supports mTLS using customer-provided certs or our managed certs. Owner: Ben (technical).

2) At-rest: Default is AES-256-GCM for persistent model artifacts and snapshots. Logs are encrypted at-rest with AES-256 and can be encrypted with separate KEKs if you choose BYOK. Owner: Ben.

3) KMS/HSM: We support AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault (Cloud KMS integr) and can integrate with external HSMs via our transit gateway (partner HSM integrations available — we work with KeyFort and Cryptonix). For payments workloads we typically recommend an HSM-backed KMS with envelope encryption and customer-controlled root KEKs. Owner: Priyom (contracts/ops).

4) BYOK workflow: Steps (high level): key import or external wrapping -> assign key policy -> configure deployment pin -> key rotation schedule -> audit handshake. Redwood ops never have your raw key material for BYOK imports; we store wrapped KEKs under your KMS. We can provide an attestation letter for custody model; for formal HSM attestations we coordinate with the HSM partner. Owner: Priyom.

5) Audit & logs: Key usage, decrypt/encrypt events, rotation events, and KMS API calls are logged. We can offload logs to your CloudWatch/Stackdriver or a secure syslog endpoint. Standard retention is 90 days in hosted; for Dedicated/Private we offer customizable retention (30d–7y) and can set up a dedicated streaming export. Owner: Ben.

6) Data residency & retention: Private deployments are customer-controlled for backups — you choose region and storage. Hosted customers can pin region for data residency; we'll add a SLA clause for region pinning in enterprise contracts. Owner: Priyom.

Action items + timeline (proposed):
- Ben: technical deep-dive (answer follow-up on envelope format, CSR for mTLS, and HSM partner integration checklist) — Wed 5/16 10:00 PT (suggested)
- Priyom: provide contract language examples for BYOK/HSM, attestation template, and SOW addendum — deliver by Fri 5/18 EOD
- Marissa: consolidate security runbook and follow up with your security committee — target Mon 5/21

Please confirm the Wed slot if that works and we'll send a calendar invite+Zoom. If you prefer Thu, Ben can make Thu 5/17 14:00 PT as well.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference

Sara — quick technical clarifications from my side ahead of the deep-dive: 

- mTLS: for private deployments we support client certs pinned to the instance. If you bring your own certs we accept a PKCS#12 upload or a CSR-based flow.
- Envelope format: we use a standard envelope with a data key (AES-256-GCM) encrypted under a KEK from your KMS (RSA-OAEP or KMS-native wrapping).
- HSMs: KeyFort offers remote HSM-backed signing and key wrapping; integration is via our transit gateway using an HSM connector. That preserves FIPS 140-2/3 boundaries.
- Logs: we can include per-request KMS event IDs in the token exchange metadata; please indicate whether you need a push to CloudWatch or a pull API.

For the deep-dive, Ben (me) will cover mTLS CSR steps, envelope examples, and the HSM connector checklist. If you can pre-fill the retention period in the spreadsheet (we recommend 1 year for most telemetry, 7 years for payments audit copies) that will help scope cost.

—Ben
